for: auditor adoption into the ledger (AM6 F25 LOW, mitigated)
finding: two parallel builder sessions on one branch caused a non-fast-forward push; resolved cleanly (duplicates dropped, additive record kept, divergence typed — b916dc63e)

protocol.1_fetch_before_push: EVERY push is preceded by `git fetch origin queue/dev12_r7`; on divergence the session rebases/merges BEFORE pushing (practiced this session: a077ff2d2 diverged from the parallel crowllm registration round; resolved by resetting to their tip and re-committing only the additive record)
protocol.2_duplicate_supersession: when a parallel session's deeper measurement exists on the remote, the later session DROPS its duplicate code edits and keeps only additive records — never both implementations (Art. LXIV: one live implementation per question)
protocol.3_credential_ownership: the session that admits a credential to the vault owns its registration for that round (crowllm: the parallel session owned the ProviderSpec/allowlist/calibration; the first session owned the window-state record and the vault admission)
protocol.4_divergence_typing: conflicting measurements between sessions are TYPED, never silently reconciled (the v4.1-flash 200-OK vs 503-dead divergence is kept in eval/crowllm_window_state_r11.json with both sessions attributed)
protocol.5_scope_stamps: commit messages state which session owns which surface (llm_registry/model_routing/transport_capability/eval-run vs AM5 eval surfaces) so a merge reviewer can see non-overlap at a glance
protocol.6_audit_branch_untouched: both builder sessions stay off audit/* (F21 guard) — the auditor writes via REST only

acceptance_tracking: 0 conflicting parallel pushes next round = the auditor's D5 acceptance; the fetch-before-push rule above is the mechanical safeguard
